item.title: MiniMax-H3 distilled comparison
item.description:
Recently we’ve released a lot of merged checkpoints for MiniMax-H3, linked in the table below. Below we compare some example renders between all of them with a full 20 timestep render. The results are not straightforward and we didn’t find any numerical measures that convey anything meaningful.

Checkpoint Steps Sampler Shift (video / audio) I2V time Ref2V time
Base 20 res_multistep 12 / 3 195.2s 241.6s
DMAD 4 dmad 12 / 2 58.3s 65.3s
DMAD 8 dmad 12 / 2 90.1s 111.6s
PDMD 4 pdmd 12 / 3 56.5s 72.9s
lightx2v 4 lightx2v 6 / 3 57.7s 66.8s
lightx2v 8 lightx2v 6 / 3 89.8s 110.3s

I2V times use the rally car shot and Ref2V times use the elf archer shot. We timed warm requests on an RTX 4080.

item.title: Faster MiniMax-H3 with Sage and Sparse Attention
item.description:
MiniMax-H3 generates video and audio together, and due to its large model size it is the most attention-heavy model in our lineup. Attention is well known to be the most expensive part of inference: attention grows with the square of the token count.

In this post we follow two changes to the attention of MiniMax-H3. Warm measurements on RTX 4080:

1344×768, 124 frames, I2V Wall time Denoise Speedup vs Nox cuDNN
Nox, cuDNN 147.8s 128.1s –
Nox, SageAttention 84.3s 64.5s 1.75×
Nox, Sage + 15% raster routing 66.7s 46.8s 2.22×
Nox, Sage + 15% Nox sparse 66.7s 46.7s 2.22×
Nox, Sage + Veda 44 tiles 68.1s 47.9s 2.17×

Quantizing the kernel with SageAttention

MiniMax-H3 has 1344×768 as its official 16:9 canvas. At that shape, cuDNN flash attention is close to the FP16 Tensor Core roof. SageAttention takes a different route: it keeps attention dense, but moves QKᵀ to INT8 and P·V to FP8. The lower-precision Tensor Core paths have a much higher throughput roof on Ada.

item.title: Benchmarking Nox against ComfyUI
item.description: A speedup is only meaningful if both sides did the same work. It is easy to make an inference engine look fast: run fewer steps, drop to a lower resolution, swap in a smaller or more aggressively quantized checkpoint, or compare a warm process against a cold one. We wanted the Nox benchmarks to be immune to all of that, so this post explains how the comparison is set up and then shows every output from the latest run next to its ComfyUI counterpart.
